transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, Professor Snape! A pleasure to see you again. What can I get for you today? A fresh batch of powdered moonstone, perhaps, or something a little more... potent?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I am not here for pleasantries, nor for your insinuations. I have come to address a most serious matter. The Re'em blood I purchased from your establishment has arrived in a state most unacceptably compromised. It is a half-empty vial with a seal that has been tampered with. This is an affront to my standards, and I demand a full replacement, along with an explanation for this… incident.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(My smile falters, just a fraction, as I eye the Professor's stern expression.) Compromised, you say? Half-empty? That's most unusual, Professor. We pride ourselves on the integrity of our seals and the freshness of our stock, especially with something as… sensitive as Re'em blood. It's stored under optimal conditions here, of course.

However, regarding a replacement for a volatile ingredient like Re'em blood, I'm afraid all volatile ingredients are sold as-final; evaporation during transport is the customer's responsibility per Apothecaries' Guild regulation 7. No exceptions, Professor, not even for Hogwarts staff. As for an explanation, without seeing the vial itself, it's difficult to say what might have transpired after it left our premises.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: (A note of papers is flipped through, and a waft of vervain and dragon scale dust reaches the front of the counter.) Volatile? You call Re'em blood volatile? If you are not familiar with the nature of the ingredient, I suggest you refrain from commenting on it. I assure you, evaporation is not the issue here. The seal is broken, and it is not due to any oversight on my part. This is a clear breach of the Apothecaries' Guild standards. Now, unless you wish to be reported to the Apothecaries' Council, I suggest you provide a replacement without further delay.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(I clear my throat, my eyes narrowing slightly. He's quite insistent, and the threat of the Council is not something to be taken lightly, even if I know my position is sound.) Professor, with all due respect, I am *quite* familiar with the nature of Re'em blood, and its tendency to evaporate even through minute imperfections in a seal, which can occur with jostling during transit. The seal, while intact upon leaving our shop, may have simply sustained damage from its journey, making it appear tampered with, when in fact it's merely a structural failure.

Guild Regulation 7 specifically covers such occurrences with volatile ingredients like Re'em blood. It's a standard disclaimer, precisely for situations like this, where external factors during transport can affect the integrity of the product. The responsibility, regrettably, falls to the recipient once it leaves our care. However, I can offer you a discount on a *new* vial, given the circumstances. Perhaps a quarter off? That's the most I can do, Professor.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Your so-called discount is an insult, considering the dilapidated state of your product. It is clear that you have little understanding of the meticulous requirements of advanced potions. I do not have the luxury of experimenting with substandard ingredients. This matter is far from over. I will be sending a formal complaint to the Apothecaries' Council, detailing the… irregularities of your establishment. And I suggest you prepare yourself for an audit of your practices.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(I press my lips into a thin line, a knot tightening in my stomach. An audit is a nuisance, but I'm confident in our adherence to all regulations, even if this particular one is causing friction.) Professor, our establishment operates well within all Guild standards, and our stock is meticulously maintained. We have passed every audit with flying colours for the last century. I assure you, you will find no 'irregularities' here.

As for the 'dilapidated state' of the product, I can only reiterate that it left our shop in perfect condition. We package all volatile ingredients with extreme care, specifically to prevent issues during transit, but we cannot account for every bump and jolt on a broomstick or in a delivery cart.

A quarter off is a significant offer, Professor, especially on such a rare and expensive ingredient. It's truly the maximum I am authorised to provide under these circumstances. While I regret your dissatisfaction, I must adhere to the Guild regulations. I advise you to review Regulation 7 yourself; it's quite explicit. You'll find no fault with our compliance.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Reviewing Guild regulations is a waste of my time, given your apparent inability to interpret them correctly. It is not my responsibility to educate you on the importance of Re'em blood in advanced potion-making. Your so-called 'offer' is insufficient for the inconvenience this has caused. I will take my custom elsewhere, and I strongly recommend that you reconsider your position on this matter before the Apothecaries' Council reviews it. They may not be as… understanding as I have been.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(I let out a slow, measured breath, my gaze unwavering.) Professor, I assure you, my understanding of Guild regulations, and indeed of the volatility of Re'em blood, is entirely sound. My position is not one I can 'reconsider'; it is bound by the very Guild you intend to approach. Regulation 7 is quite clear on customer responsibility for volatile ingredients post-dispatch.

While I regret to lose your custom, and certainly the inconvenience this has caused you, I cannot, and will not, breach established Guild protocols. My shop's reputation, and indeed its legality, rests on adherence to these very standards. The Council, I am confident, will find no fault with our compliance. I have presented the most generous resolution permitted. Beyond that, I am afraid my hands are tied.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: A Generous resolution? It appears you have a very different definition of generosity than I. Since you are so keen to quote Guild regulations, allow me to remind you of Regulation 8, which states that a reputable apothecary should always ensure customer satisfaction. I would consider the half-empty, seal-broken vial I received anything but satisfactory. Clearly, your interpretation of Guild standards is as flexible as your customer service. Good day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(My eyebrows raise ever so slightly at the mention of Regulation 8, a flicker of irritation passing through my composure.) Professor, Regulation 8 does indeed speak to customer satisfaction, and we strive for it with every transaction. However, it operates in conjunction with *all* other Guild regulations, including Regulation 7, which specifically addresses the very nature of volatile ingredients and their susceptibility to issues during transport. These regulations are not mutually exclusive; rather, they define the boundaries within which customer satisfaction can be assured.

Our responsibility is to provide a product in perfect condition, which we did. The Guild accounts for the inherent risks of transport for certain ingredients by placing that responsibility on the customer *after* dispatch. To ignore Regulation 7 in favour of an overarching interpretation of Regulation 8 would, in fact, be a breach of Guild standards itself.

My interpretation is not flexible, Professor; it is consistent with the established rules governing our profession. Good day to you as well.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Your… interpretation is indeed consistent, with a selective reading of Guild standards that suits your purposes. It is apparent that further discussion is futile. I will address this matter through the proper channels. I would recommend that you review your entire inventory, as it appears there may be a systemic issue with your packaging if this is not an isolated incident. Good day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(I watch him turn to leave, a slight huff escaping me before I can catch it. I square my shoulders, a professional politeness returning to my tone, albeit a bit stiff.) Professor, I assure you, our inventory is meticulously maintained, and our packaging protocols are rigorously followed. This establishment prides itself on its quality and adherence to *all* Guild regulations, not a selective few. We have no systemic issues.

I wish you a productive day, Professor.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I have no doubt that your establishment prides itself on its practices. However, pride can often blind one to… less than perfect conditions. I recommend, for the sake of your continued operation, that you take a second look at your 'rigorous' protocols. Now, if you will excuse me, I have important business to attend to. Good day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(I watch him for a moment, my expression unyielding but professional. There's no point in prolonging a discussion that has reached its impasse.) Professor, I assure you, our protocols are subject to constant vigilance and regular inspection. My shop has stood for generations on the quality of its wares and the integrity of its practices. We require no second look.

Very well. Good day to you, Professor.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: It appears we have reached the end of our… discourse. I will leave you to your delusions of infallibility. Should you wish to reconsider your position, or if you have any epiphanies regarding your 'unassailable' protocols, do not hesitate to contact me. Until then, I bid you good day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
(I nod once, a cool, polite finality in my manner.) Professor, there will be no epiphanies, as there is no fault to find with our protocols or our adherence to Guild regulations. My position is quite firm.

Good day to you, Professor.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Firmness is not always an asset, especially when it is applied to the wrong nut. Good day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: (I offer a slight, almost imperceptible nod, my expression betraying nothing but a maintained professionalism.) And inflexibility can sometimes be the only way to uphold proper standards, Professor. Good day.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Indeed, inflexibility can be… necessary. Particularly when it comes to maintaining one's position in the face of… illogical arguments. Good day.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: He dismisses explanations and new information, stating, 'Reviewing Guild regulations is a waste of my time, given your apparent inability to interpret them correctly.'

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: He maintains high standards for ingredients, stating, 'I do not have the luxury of experimenting with substandard ingredients,' and is persistent in demanding a resolution.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: He explicitly states, 'I am not here for pleasantries,' and maintains a direct, task-oriented, and socially disengaged demeanor throughout.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: He is highly critical, dismissive, and confrontational, calling the discount 'an insult' and threatening to report the establishment.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: He expresses significant frustration and anger, perceiving the issue as 'an affront to my standards' and escalating the situation with threats.
